title: Unbiased Locally Private Estimator for Polynomials of Laplacian Variables

problem.claim: Locally private data contains Laplacian noise, which introduces bias when non-linear functions are computed from it.

gap.claim: Existing locally private data handling does not directly avoid the bias arising in polynomial or other non-linear calculations.

contributions.claim: A recursive algorithm debiases polynomial functions computed from locally differentially private data.
The algorithm has calculation time O(r n log n), where r is the polynomial degree and n is the number of users.
The method is evaluated on k-star counting and variance estimation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was evaluated on k-star counting and variance estimation against state-of-the-art algorithms.
The authors report that the method eliminates bias and provides at least 100 times more accuracy than previous works.

narrative_sequence.summary: Local differential privacy adds Laplacian noise before data is submitted to a central server.
The noise causes bias when non-linear functions are computed from the submitted data.
The work proposes a recursive debiasing algorithm with calculation time O(r n log n).
The method is evaluated on k-star counting and variance estimation against state-of-the-art algorithms.
The authors report bias elimination and at least 100 times greater accuracy than previous works.

source_observation.claim: Noise introduced for local privacy can bias downstream non-linear calculations.

interpretation.claim: Privacy-preserving transformations should be analyzed for their effect on the estimands or computations that follow.

application.claim: When using locally private data for polynomial statistics, consider an explicit debiasing procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach applies beyond the stated polynomial setting or evaluation problems.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify privacy parameters or assumptions.
The abstract does not provide algorithmic details or theoretical guarantees.
The abstract does not describe datasets, evaluation settings, or the basis of the reported accuracy comparison.
